items.title: Section: Bestowing Ease — Temporary Relief From the Five Hindrances, and Two Stories of Mind Transforming Circumstance

items.zh: 能施安樂者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，說正法時，與聽法者饒益身心輕安之樂，令離諸蓋，專心聽法。暫時方便，而非究竟。
items.en: Bestowing ease: buddhas and bodhisattvas, resting on mastery over concentration, when expounding the true teaching, grant listeners a beneficial ease of body and mind, freeing them from the hindrances so they may listen with focused attention. This is a temporary expedient, not an ultimate one.

items.zh: 又令諸界互相違變能為損害、非人所行、災癘、疾疫皆得息滅。是名能施安樂。
items.en: They are also able to bring to rest the harm caused by the four elements turning against one another within the body, the doings of non-human spirits, and epidemics and plagues. This is called bestowing ease.

items.title: Radiating Great Light — Two Kinds, and Summoning Every Realm to Assembly

items.zh: 放大光明者，謂佛菩薩依定自在，以神通力，身放光明。或有一光往十方面無量無數諸世界中，令惡趣等一切有情息彼眾苦。
items.en: Radiating great light: buddhas and bodhisattvas, resting on mastery over concentration, radiate light from their bodies through miraculous power. A single ray of this light may travel to immeasurable, uncountable worlds throughout the ten directions, bringing all beings in the miserable realms and elsewhere to the cessation of their many sufferings.

items.zh: 或有一光往諸天界，令大威德天、龍、藥叉、健達縛、阿素洛、揭路荼、緊捺洛、牟呼洛伽等住自宮中，蒙光覺悟，皆來集會。
items.en: Or a single ray of light may travel to the heavenly realms, so that mighty gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, each dwelling in their own palace, are awakened by this light and all gather together in assembly.

items.title: Radiating Light Closes All Eighteen Transformations of the Power to Transmute

items.zh: 或有一光往十方面無量無數諸世界中，令住他方世界菩薩蒙光覺悟，皆來集會。以要言之，諸如來等能放無量無數品類種種光明，能作無量無數世界無量無數諸有情類無量無數利益之事。
items.en: Or a single ray of light may travel to immeasurable, uncountable worlds throughout the ten directions, so that bodhisattvas dwelling in other world-systems are awakened by this light and all gather together in assembly. ... In brief, the Tathāgatas are able to radiate immeasurable, uncountable kinds of light of every variety, accomplishing immeasurable, uncountable acts of benefit for immeasurable, uncountable beings across immeasurable, uncountable worlds.

items.zh: 當知如是一切能變神境智通品類差別，一一分別無量無數。由此神通，能轉所餘有自性物令成餘物，故名能變神境智通。
items.en: It should be understood that all such distinct varieties of the power to transmute are, if distinguished one by one, truly immeasurable and uncountable. Because this miraculous power is able to change any remaining thing possessing its own nature into another thing, it is called the power to transmute.

items.title: Section: Conjuring Opens — Creating Body, Realm, and Speech From Nothing at All

items.zh: 云何能化神境智通品類差別？謂若略說，無事而有，是名為化。能以化心，隨其所欲，造作種種未曾有事，故名能化神境智通。
items.en: What are the distinct varieties of the power to conjure? In brief: bringing into being what was not there at all is called conjuring. Being able, through a conjuring mind, to produce whatever unprecedented thing is wished for — this is called the power to conjure.

items.zh: 此復多種。或化為身及化為境，或化為語。
items.en: This, too, has many varieties: conjuring a body, conjuring a realm or object, and conjuring speech.

items.title: Conjured Bodies — Sometimes Countless Copies of Oneself, Sometimes Utterly Unlike

items.zh: 或化為身及化為境者，化似自身，或不相似；化似他身，或不相似。
items.en: Regarding conjuring a body or a realm: a conjured body may resemble one's own form, or not resemble it; it may resemble another's form, or not resemble it.

items.zh: 又所化身，若自、若他，或似、不似，唯能化作與根相似根所依處，而非實根。復能化作相似境界。謂飲食等，末尼、真珠、琉璃寶等，所有色、香、味、觸所攝外資生具。
items.en: Moreover, whether such a conjured body resembles oneself or another, whether similar or dissimilar, it can only be conjured with the outward appearance of the sense faculties' physical basis, never the genuine sense faculties themselves. They are also able to conjure resembling environments — food and drink, gemstones, pearls, lapis lazuli, and every other outward provision comprising form, scent, taste, and texture.

items.zh: 若彼相似，若異於彼，隨其所欲一切能化。

items.title: Conjured Bodies Across Every Realm — From Gods to Buddhas, One Form or Countless at Once

items.zh: 又所化身與己同類，非一眾多種種差別。或作天、龍、藥叉、健達縛、阿素洛、揭路荼、緊捺洛、牟呼洛伽色像，或作人、傍生、鬼、那洛迦色像，或作聲聞、獨覺、菩薩、如來色像。
items.en: A conjured body of the same general kind as oneself may take countless distinct forms. One may conjure the form of a deva, nāga, yakṣa, gandharva, asura, garuḍa, kiṃnara, or mahoraga; the form of a human, animal, ghost, or hell-being; or the form of a hearer, solitary buddha, bodhisattva, or Tathāgata.

items.zh: 若所化身與菩薩身極相似者，名所化身與自相似。若不爾者，名所化身非自相似。又所化身與他同類亦有多種。若作天身，與彼天身極相似者，名所化身與他相似；若不爾者，名所化身非他相似。如作天身，乃至佛身，當知亦爾。
云何此中化作多身？謂佛菩薩於十方面無量無數諸世界中，一時化作種種形類，能為無量無數有情作利益事。
items.en: What does it mean to conjure many bodies at once? Buddhas and bodhisattvas, throughout immeasurable, uncountable worlds in the ten directions, simultaneously conjure every variety of form, thereby accomplishing acts of benefit for immeasurable, uncountable sentient beings.

items.title: Conjured Forms Persist or Cease as Needed, Matched to Each Being's Own Readiness

items.zh: 如是所化種種形類，於中或有諸佛菩薩雖滅度後，由住持力而故隨轉；或有暫時作利益已，化事便息。
items.en: Among these various conjured forms, some, even after the buddhas and bodhisattvas who conjured them have passed into final nirvāṇa, continue to function through their sustaining power; others, having accomplished a temporary benefit, simply cease once that work is done.

items.title: Conjured Realms — Sometimes Only to Be Seen, Sometimes Genuinely Usable

items.zh: 又佛菩薩或作化事，唯令眾生覩見而已，如幻所作不堪受用。或復化作飲食、衣服、末尼、真珠、琉璃、螺貝、壁玉、珊瑚、車乘等事，與實無異。如是所作財食眾具，令諸眾生常得受用。
items.en: Buddhas and bodhisattvas sometimes conjure a display meant only for beings to look upon, illusion-like and incapable of genuine use. At other times they conjure food, clothing, gemstones, pearls, lapis lazuli, coral, or carriages that are no different from the genuine article — such conjured wealth, food, and provisions can be put to lasting, ordinary use by any being who receives them.

items.zh: 是名化身及化境界。或化為語者，或有化語妙音相應，或有化語廣音具足，或有化語繫屬於自，或有化語繫屬於他，或有化語無所繫屬，或有化語宣說正法言詞所攝，或有化語誨責放逸言詞所攝。

items.title: Section: Conjured Speech's Eight Qualities of Perfection — And Three Disciples Each Criticised for How They Taught

items.zh: 妙音相應者，謂佛菩薩所說化語，其聲深遠如雲雷音，其聲和雅如頻迦音，能感眾心，甚可愛樂。又此化語，圓上、微妙、顯了、易解、樂聞、無逆、無依、無盡。
items.en: Wondrous in tone: conjured speech whose sound is as deep and far-reaching as thunder in the clouds, yet as gentle and refined as the call of the kalaviṅka bird, moving the hearts of the assembly with genuine delight. This conjured speech is, moreover, supreme, wondrous, clear, easily understood, delightful to hear, never contrary to the listener, free of any self-interested motive, and inexhaustible.

blocks.text: The last transformations, then "conjuring": creating what did not exist. A short passage (0493a26) is untranslated.

"When expounding the true teaching, they grant listeners a beneficial ease of body and mind, freeing them from the hindrances so they may listen with focus. This is a temporary expedient, not an ultimate one." They also calm illness, spirits, and epidemics.
"A single ray may travel to immeasurable worlds", awakening gods, nāgas, and others, or bodhisattvas in other worlds, who gather to hear. Master Cháng Bǎi: two kinds of light.

"Bringing into being what was not there at all is called conjuring." Venerable Miào Jìng: "there was nothing, and suddenly there is." Conjuring has three kinds: bodies, realms or objects, and speech. Master Cháng Bǎi: mind is not mentioned because it cannot be conjured.

They may resemble one's own form or another's; but "only the outward appearance of the sense faculties' physical basis is conjured, never the genuine faculties". They may take the form of any being, "one body or countless at once". Some persist after the conjurer's final nirvāṇa; others vanish when their task is done.
"Sometimes a display only to be looked at, illusion-like; at other times food, clothing, gems" that can actually be used.

Eight perfections of conjured speech: "deep and far-reaching as thunder, yet gentle as the kalaviṅka bird's call", supreme, clear, easily understood, delightful, never contrary, "free of any self-interested motive", inexhaustible. Venerable Miào Jìng: "I say this to benefit you, not to make you believe in me."

quiz.q: Bestowing ease frees listeners from hindrances — "temporary, not ultimate." What do the masters say?
options: both: truly removing the hindrances depends on one's own effort — otherwise ordinary beings would already be buddhas
quiz.why: "Freeing them from the hindrances so they may listen with focused attention. This is a temporary expedient, not an ultimate one." Master Cháng Bǎi: finally removing the five hindrances still depends on one's own effort; if powers could remove them, ordinary beings would have been buddhas long ago. Venerable Miào Jìng: it doesn't ultimately make them cut off the hindrances — cutting them takes your own effort.

quiz.q: "Radiating great light through miraculous power." What two kinds of light does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish?
options: constant light always emitted, and light emitted by power to gather beings
quiz.why: "Radiating great light: buddhas and bodhisattvas … radiate light from their bodies through miraculous power." Master Cháng Bǎi: there are two kinds — constant light, which buddhas and bodhisattvas always emit; and light emitted through power when there's a special task.

quiz.q: "Bringing into being what was not there is called conjuring." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: what wasn't there suddenly appears — from nothing to something
quiz.why: "In brief: bringing into being what was not there at all is called conjuring." Venerable Miào Jìng: there was no such thing, and suddenly there is — that's 化; from nothing to something is 化.

quiz.q: Conjuring covers "body, realm, or speech" — why not mind? What do the masters say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: consciousness is karmic result and can't be conjured; Miào Jìng, citing the Saṃdhinirmocana: mind is cognizing by nature — not conjurable
quiz.why: "This, too, has many varieties: conjuring a body, conjuring a realm or object, and conjuring speech." Master Cháng Bǎi: mind isn't mentioned because consciousness is a karmic result that can't be conjured — only surface objects can. Venerable Miào Jìng: the Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra says mind can't be conjured; it's a cognizing thing.

quiz.q: A conjured body has "only the appearance of the faculties' basis, never genuine faculties." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: only the outward organs — real faculties come from karmic result
quiz.why: "It can only be conjured with the outward appearance of the sense faculties' physical basis, never the genuine sense faculties themselves." Master Cháng Bǎi: the power to conjure can only produce outward organs, not real faculties; real faculties are produced by karmic results.

quiz.q: Some conjurations are "only to be seen, illusion-like, unusable." What example does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: an illusionist pulls out a fish — but it can't be eaten
quiz.why: "Buddhas and bodhisattvas sometimes conjure a display meant only for beings to look upon, illusion-like and incapable of genuine use." Venerable Miào Jìng: an illusionist reaches out and produces a fish, but that fish can't be used — it's illusion, not a real fish. (The note says bread.)

quiz.q: Conjured speech is "never contrary to the listener (無逆)." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: too much would weary you — so he knows the measure
quiz.why: "This conjured speech is, moreover, supreme, wondrous, clear, easily understood, delightful to hear, never contrary to the listener, free of any self-interested motive, and inexhaustible." Venerable Miào Jìng: if he said too much, you might grow weary — so he knows the measure.
